Anya: Quick heads-up — I sketched swimlanes for Optimize prioritization. Goal: separate infra-mandatory work (batching infra, KV caching) from high-touch customer pilots (quant recs, eval alerts). Need alignment on what we treat as 'MUST ship for Q2 pilot' vs 'NICE to have'.
Mike: Can you paste the swimlane matrix?
Anya: Sure — pasted below. TL;DR: infra pieces needed for stable pilot: batching API + KV cache + rollout flags. Customer-facing recommendations (quant profiles, per-route heuristics, eval-triggered alerts) can be phased.
Anya: ```
Swimlane A (Infra, Q2 must): batching API v1, KV prefix caching, route-level rate limits, rollout flags
Swimlane B (Pilot UX, Q2 defer->Q3): quant recommendation UI, per-customer profiles, eval-to-alert plumbing
Swimlane C (Ops/tooling, Q3+): adaptive batching tuning, econ signals for fallback, long-term quant cookbook
```
Priya: Looks sane. For the pilot customers (Acorn & Streamline) they care most about predictable latency and cost. If we don't surface quant recs in pilot, is that OK?
Seb: Short answer: yes — we can run automated quant experiments offline and provide a recommended config to pilots without a full UI. But we need deterministic rollout hooks so we can revert if quality regresses.
Jordan: Agree with Seb. Also we should add one small telemetry gate in Swimlane A: a per-route token-cost estimate emitted to console so customers can see impact without digging into traces.
Mike: That token-cost estimate is low-effort and high-value. +1.
Anya: Noted. Proposed acceptance criteria for Swimlane A pilot readiness:
- batching API handles 200 concurrent requests with <=50ms extra per-request latency in 95th percentile
- KV cache hit-rate >= 30% on prefix workloads in pilot dataset
- rollout flags exist and tested in Canary with automatic fallback to hosted variant
- basic cost estimate emitted for each route
Priya: For Swimlane B (quant & eval alerts) what are the minimal hooks we need?
Anya: Minimal: a batch job that runs candidate quantizations against a holdout prompt set and emits simple metrics (tokens saved, measured LM score delta) + an eval-alert rule that triggers on regression > X (TBD).
Seb: For X I'd suggest 2% downstream metric delta for high-sensitivity customers, 5% for broader default. We can param by customer.
Jordan: Also include a toggle that maps alert->auto-rollforward only for internal pilots; don't let it auto-change prod configs for enterprise customers without human approval.
Anya: Good call. Any objections to ordering: finish Swimlane A infra + telemetry (2 weeks), run offline quant experiments (1 week), deliver basic quant recs to pilot customers as a config (1 week), then light UI for recs in Q3?
Mike: That schedule seems optimistic but doable if we focus scope. We should bake in a 1-week buffer for debugging rollout issues.
Priya: I'll coordinate pilots & acceptance testing with Acorn/Streamline — can we add a checklist item for data retention/KMS for private tenants? Some of their security folks asked about logs.
Anya: Added. Swimlane A acceptance now includes KMS policy review and audit-log sampling.
deploy-bot: CI:batching-infra #342 merged into release/canary — runs green ✅
Seb: Nice. With that merged, can we get an internal canary next week? I want to validate KV hit patterns with real traffic.
Anya: Yes — I'll schedule canary Monday and loop in SRE for monitoring dashboards.
Mike: One more ask: product pricing impact note. If quant recs are adopted, legal needs wording for savings estimates. Priya, can you draft a short blurb for customer comms?
Priya: Yep — will do. Draft ready by Thu and share in this thread. :memo:
Anya: Thanks all. Outcome: align on Swimlane A as Q2 pilot gate, Swimlane B as targeted pilot deliverable without full UI, Swimlane C deferred. I'll convert this thread into a Confluence checklist and assign owners.
